turns.text: LANTERN (CVN-221-02) status, 02-Mar-2026. Phase II, open-label, two-cohort study of CVN-221 (oral selective FGFR2 inhibitor) in previously treated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Cohort A = FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, Cohort B = other FGFR2 alterations (activating mutations, amplifications). Primary endpoint ORR by BICR per RECIST 1.1. 14 subjects dosed so far, all under protocol v2.0 at 160 mg QD continuous, 28-day cycles. Five sites active (101 Calder Cancer Center, 102 St. Aldric Medical Center, 103 Lakeshore University Hospital, 104 Pinecrest Oncology Institute, 105 Bayridge Regional Cancer Center); site 106 Mercer Valley Health still in contracting. Enrollment target is 84 (Cohort A 48, Cohort B 36). Database lock target 30-Nov-2026. Hyperphosphatemia signal: 3 of 14 subjects with Grade 3 events (101-002, 102-003, 104-005). Ilse Varga (medical monitor) wants Amendment 1 to lower the starting dose.

turns.text: OK. Now help me with the rationale paragraph for Amendment 1. Proposal from Ilse: drop the starting dose from 160 mg to 120 mg QD, still continuous. Dose level -1 becomes 80 mg and level -2 becomes 60 mg (under v2.0 they were 120 mg and 80 mg). Also start sevelamer when serum phosphate exceeds 5.5 mg/dL instead of the current 7.0 mg/dL trigger.

Draft rationale (Section 1.3, Amendment 1): 'Among the first 14 subjects treated at 160 mg QD, 3 (21.4%) experienced CTCAE v5.0 Grade 3 hyperphosphatemia, and 5 (35.7%) required dose interruption within Cycle 1. Preliminary PK indicates steady-state AUC at 160 mg exceeds the exposure associated with maximal FGFR2 target inhibition in the Phase I population by approximately 1.6-fold. Consistent with the on-target mechanism of FGFR inhibition, the starting dose is reduced to 120 mg QD continuous (28-day cycles), with dose level -1 at 80 mg and -2 at 60 mg. Phosphate-lowering therapy (sevelamer) will be initiated at serum phosphate >5.5 mg/dL (previously >7.0 mg/dL).' Suggest you have Rohan confirm the 1.6-fold figure before it goes to Meridian; I took it from the PK slide you shared, not from a final report.

turns.text: Can you calculate Cycle 2 dose intensity for 101-011? Planned 120 mg QD for 28 days. She held doses on days 9 to 11 for Grade 2 stomatitis and resumed at 120 mg on day 12. No other missed doses per the diary.

Planned Cycle 2 dose: 120 mg x 28 days = 3,360 mg. Doses missed on days 9, 10 and 11 = 3 days, so 25 days x 120 mg = 3,000 mg received. Relative dose intensity = 3,000 / 3,360 = 89.3%. This is above the 80% threshold the SAP uses for the 'adequate exposure' sensitivity analysis, so 101-011 stays in that population for Cycle 2. If her diary later shows a vomited dose, it still counts as taken per SAP section 9.2.

Under v3.0 Table 6-2, 120 mg is level 0 and 80 mg is level -1, and Section 6.4 requires a one-level reduction at phosphate >9.0 mg/dL, so 120 -> 80 mg QD is correct for 105-003 (CTCAE v5.0 Hyperphosphatemia, Grade 3). If phosphate exceeds 9.0 mg/dL again at 80 mg, the next level is 60 mg (level -2); a third occurrence means discontinuation.

turns.text: How should sites handle subjects mid-cycle when they switch to 21/7?

turns.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
turns.text: With Cohort B at 48, what precision do we get on ORR if the true rate is 30%?

Using the normal approximation, the 95% CI half-width is 1.96 x sqrt(0.30 x 0.70 / 48) = 1.96 x 0.0661 = 0.130, i.e. about +/-13.0 percentage points (roughly 17%-43%). With the original 36 it was 1.96 x sqrt(0.21/36) = 0.150, about +/-15.0 points. For the CSR, Rohan will report exact Clopper-Pearson intervals, which are slightly wider and asymmetric: for 14/48 (29.2%) the exact 95% CI is approximately 17.0%-44.1%.
